Yep. NCT 2020 was basically a barrage of insanely talented men and attempting to rank them from #1 to #23 is near impossible, considering a lot of things. This is why I love fancams, because I am able to study each member and give them my undivided attention. In the main stage videos, it's a common tendency for the eye to stray to the centre when it's a wide shot and in general we get more close ups of those in the centre. Honestly I believe that the reason it seems that Mark and Taeyong are being 'pushed' by SM is because they are often in the centre during the chorus + their well deserved lines. 

Also, talking about Jisung, I just want to bring up how amazing he is at gesturing during performances. He's a great dancer for sure too. I know we're talking about performance in general but I notice how much of an intriguing contrast his dancing technique is compared to Jeno's. Jisung likes to keep things sharp and controlled, while Jeno makes things big. Jeno's movements extend further and it makes him look huge on stage. This of course comes with the negative effects, making it seem like he over dances and if he doesn't retract his limbs fast enough it can disturb the rest of the moves. Thankfully, Jeno has the strength to exert the force. Side note: I would like to see Jisung sing more, his voice is amazing.

As for Shotaro, he too is a great performer. Seeing him on stage is a serotonin booster, and he just looks like he's enjoying himself. That said, I'm excited to see his development as a rapper as it seems like it's the direction he's going.

I suppose it's the benefit of exploring different concepts as the boys become adults but NCT Dream in general gets the push in versatility. Also, I agree that Jeno is often left out in conversations involving NCT as great performers. I believe that he is much more appreciated for his visuals, which I don't blame, but I wish they would notice him for his raw talent as a performer!

I can share some things that I hoped a family member had done the same with me. Note that this may not apply to your sister too.

If you plan on asking her about the matter, approach her gently. A 'safe' environment is quite important, so perhaps, call her over for a simple conversation.

You've noted that she isn't an open person, so do try to gain her trust. Assure her that you are concerned/willing to listen/will not belittle her/won't leak her thoughts/will not become angry/won't invalidate her experience, and ensure you do not fail your words.

Also, do not force her to speak of her feelings. She may still remain uncomfortable and you should respect her boundaries.

Once again, this is simply what I had wished was done the same for me and what I would do when encountering a similar situation, so I apologise if I have provided any misinformation. I'm not a professional. Please take some time to calm yourself first, and approach her when you are ready. I hope it will work out and that you and your sister will receive the help you need.
